body:
Windows cancellation now stops descendant processes in both JavaScript and Rust. Rust streaming cancellation also stops POSIX workers that ignore termination after their shell exits.

Fixes #205. Unblocks [link-assistant/agent#320](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/320).

## Changes

- Stop Windows process trees with `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` before terminating the parent. Keep direct-child fallback termination and optional trace diagnostics. Avoid delayed JavaScript kills against potentially reused Windows PIDs.
- Preserve Rust process-group escalation through the POSIX grace period even when the shell exits first. Zero grace and explicit `SIGKILL` terminate immediately.
- Handle asynchronous stdin `EPIPE` without accumulating error listeners or listener warnings.
- Test shell and exact-argv cancellation through abort, timeout, kill, zero grace, ignored signals and iterator exit. Fixtures wait for a positive heartbeat and have finite lifetimes and explicit cleanup.
- Add Node.js 20/22/24 cancellation jobs on Windows and macOS alongside existing Linux Node, three-platform Bun and Rust coverage. Both JavaScript release paths require these regressions to pass.
- Prepare patch releases for both packages, document platform behavior, and remove the JavaScript-only parity exemption. Merge the latest default branch while preserving its signal-status changes.

If Windows `taskkill` fails or is unavailable, the fallback terminates the direct child; it cannot guarantee descendant termination in that environment.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, both original JavaScript Windows heartbeat tests failed in [run 36610911128](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/36610911128).

The expanded Rust tests were committed before the implementation. [Run 37475608185](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37475608185) reproduced surviving descendants on Windows and failed POSIX escalation on Linux and macOS. [Investigation notes and preserved logs](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-320-b2913f5b1c99/dev/log/issues/205/pulls/206/analysis/cancellation-review.md) record the errors and exact log lines.

## Verification

- Local Rust: 826 passing tests, including doctests; all features enabled with compiler/documentation warnings denied. Formatting, Clippy and API documentation passed.
- Local executable parity: all 29 features passed across Node, Bun and Rust.
- Combined cancellation and signal-status regressions: 78 passing Node tests after integrating the latest default branch.
- Full local suites after integrating the latest default branch: Bun 2,527 passed / 10 skipped; Node 622 passed / 2 skipped. JavaScript lint, formatting, types and duplication checks passed.
- Final review additionally verifies child-listener cleanup after successful Windows tree termination and fallback termination. All three isolated cleanup cases failed before the correction.
- Final CI on commit `4e4563101761471e89034d1ccb89147539dcc98d`: all 38 checks passed. [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37479906310) covers Node.js 20/22/24 and Bun across Linux, Windows and macOS; [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37479906163) passes on all three platforms. [Language parity](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37479906193), security analysis, audits, documentation and workflow checks also passed. Release jobs are skipped on pull requests as expected.
- The actual single-changeset validator and 185 release/documentation regression checks passed locally. The working tree is clean and includes the latest default branch.

Two existing default-branch dependency alerts remain open: [braces](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/security/dependabot/1) and [sprintf-js](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/security/dependabot/2). GitHub's records list no patched versions. The investigation notes preserve this limitation; the cancellation fix does not dismiss these alerts.
